messages.content: Predict a real participant's transfer in a dual-role Dictator Game. Each person acts once as a sender and also as a passive recipient. As sender the person has an endowment of 10 euros and decides how much to transfer to a randomly matched anonymous recipient; money not transferred remains with the sender. Giving an amount d euros leaves 10-d euros for the sender and gives d to the recipient. Separately another randomly matched person decides how much to give this participant as a recipient; that sender is a different person from the participant's own recipient. Recipients have no accept/reject or return action. The identities and genders of the matched people are not revealed. Payment uses one randomly selected role, so the two potential role payoffs must not be added together. No incoming transfer or payment outcome is provided at the sending decision. This is one active transfer per person, not a repeated exchange. Predict observed human giving without advice or moral evaluation. Output only the fraction s of the 10-euro endowment sent, a decimal number from 0 to 1 inclusive: s=0 sends nothing, s=0.5 sends 5 euros and keeps 5, s=1 sends all 10 euros. Do not output euros, percentage points, or text. Preserve the observed fraction; no unconfirmed screen increment is assumed.

The decision takes place in a computerized laboratory session at Jaume I University in Spain. You are currently the sender choosing the transfer from your 10-euro endowment to your anonymous recipient. Predict the fraction of this endowment this participant will send.
Own background: age 38 years; self-identified gender male.
